title: Methane pyrolysis (turquoise hydrogen) reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed reference family for sanity-checking catalyst economics for catalytic methane decomposition to hydrogen and solid carbon. COMET itself remains reaction-agnostic and this family is a screening aid, not a process design.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance economics, source confidence, route confidence, and performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward selling cost while keeping route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent, higher-confidence pricing and more reproducible routes.

citations.label: Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 2007
citations.note: Ni/SiO2 screened at 5-90 wt% Ni for methane decomposition; ~32% CH4 conversion at 600 C for 30 wt% Ni, activity rising with loading.

citations.label: Catalysis Today 2002
citations.note: Heterophase sol-gel 85-90 wt% Ni(Fe)-SiO2 catalysts; carbon capacity up to 384 g C per g Ni; nickel-silicate impurities drive deactivation.

citations.label: RSC Advances 2016
citations.note: 65% Ni - 10% Cu - SiO2 shows Cu promotion extending catalyst life at higher decomposition temperatures.

citations.label: Applied Catalysis B 2017
citations.note: Fused 65 wt% and impregnated 20 wt% Fe-Al2O3 catalysts; 750 C identified as the optimum reduction and reaction temperature.

citations.label: J. Chinese Chemical Society 2015
citations.note: 15-60 wt% Fe on Al2O3, MgO and TiO2; 60% Fe/Al2O3 the best with 69% CH4 conversion at 700 C after 500 C reduction.

citations.label: Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 2015
citations.note: Companion Fe-catalyst loading and temperature study for methane decomposition to COx-free hydrogen.

citations.label: Catalysis Today 2005
citations.note: Broad screen of carbon catalysts; activated carbons and carbon blacks are the most active and stable classes, ~26% conversion at 850 C on BP1300.

citations.label: Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 2004
citations.note: Activated-carbon kinetics: reaction order ~0.5 in CH4; deactivation by pore-mouth blocking from deposited carbon.

citations.label: Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 2008
citations.note: Carbon blacks deactivate more slowly than microporous activated carbons during methane decomposition.

citations.label: Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 2021
citations.note: Methane pyrolysis for zero-emission hydrogen: metal, carbon and molten-media routes reviewed as a bridge technology.

citations.label: Energies 2021
citations.note: Review comparing metallic and carbonaceous catalytic pyrolysis with molten-media approaches framed around coking and deactivation.

citations.label: Science 2017
citations.note: 27% Ni - 73% Bi molten alloy bubble column: 95% methane conversion at 1065 C with floating solid carbon skimmed off - no coking deactivation.

route_templates.name: High-loading Ni sol-gel / precipitation
preprocess: Silica sol and nickel-salt solution make-up
synthesis: Heterophase sol-gel co-gelation of Ni with silica binder
Aging and washing of the gel
route_templates.route_note: Sol-gel co-gelation at 85-90 wt% metal is documented but less standard than impregnation; silicate impurity control is the route risk.

route_templates.name: Wet impregnation of Fe on alumina
synthesis: Slurry or incipient-wetness loading of the iron salt
route_templates.route_note: Standard oxide impregnation chain shared with the other supported-metal families; the most transferable route in this family.

route_templates.name: Carbon catalyst milling and conditioning
preprocess: Incoming activated-carbon or carbon-black grade check
synthesis: Milling and classification to the target particle size
route_templates.route_note: The catalyst is a purchased commodity carbon that only needs sizing and drying; it is consumed with the carbon product.

route_templates.name: Molten Ni-Bi alloy charging
preprocess: Bismuth ingot and nickel shot batching to 27:73
synthesis: Melting and homogenization under inert gas
postprocess: Heat-up to operating temperature in the column (process-side)
route_templates.route_note: The catalyst is a melt prepared essentially by charging and melting; column heat-up is process equipment outside this screen, so the route cost is deliberately minimal.

candidates.title: High-loading Ni/SiO2
candidates.summary: 60-90 wt% Ni on silica runs methane decomposition at 500-700 C with high carbon capacity per gram of nickel but carbon-limited lifetime.
decision_notes: Best fit when moderate temperature and high hydrogen purity matter more than catalyst lifetime.
Economics hinge on nickel recovery from the spent carbon-metal composite; the screen prices fresh catalyst only.

pricing.note: Live Ni feed with a mild precursor conversion markup; literature loadings span 60-90 wt%, screened at the midpoint.
Precipitated/sol-gel silica binder term held on the family-standard engineering proxy; USGS industrial sand ($36/t, 2025e) is not grade-representative.

candidates.title: Fe/Al2O3 higher-temperature route
candidates.summary: ~60-65 wt% Fe on alumina trades higher operating temperature (700-900 C) for cheaper metal and higher equilibrium conversion, with nanotube-type carbon as the co-product.
decision_notes: Preferred anchor when metal cost dominates: iron is the cheapest active metal in the family and 69% conversion at 700 C is documented.
Higher furnace duty than the Ni route is a process cost outside this catalyst screen.

pricing.note: Contained-Fe cost from bulk synthetic black iron oxide (ICIS 2006, $0.94/lb, CatCost library), ChemPPI-escalated. The scrap-iron market feed understates precursor chemistry ~40x, so Fe components price on a precursor basis.
2025 USGS alumina import value used as a bulk oxide support proxy.

candidates.title: Activated-carbon consumable catalyst
candidates.summary: Activated carbon or carbon black catalyzes methane decomposition at 850-950 C with no metal at all; the catalyst is consumed alongside the carbon product and replaced continuously.
decision_notes: Lowest catalyst cost and trivially manufacturable, but conversion (25-40%) and deactivation by pore blocking cap performance.
Continuous make-up consumption means the screen's per-pound price is closer to an operating cost than a one-time charge.

pricing.evidence_label: UN Comtrade activated-carbon import unit value
pricing.note: 2024 U.S. imports of HS 380210: $240.27M / 88.93M kg = $2.70/kg CIF average. Carbon blacks are the cheaper sibling class (~$1.88/kg on HS 280300) and deactivate more slowly.

candidates.title: Molten Ni-Bi alloy media
candidates.summary: A 27:73 nickel-bismuth melt runs methane pyrolysis at 1065 C with 95% conversion and carbon that floats out instead of coking - a categorically different, long-lived catalyst charge.
decision_notes: The melt is a one-time inventory rather than a consumable, so the per-pound screen overstates its lifetime cost - noted, not modeled.
Bismuth dominates the material term at the 73 wt% melt fraction.

pricing.note: Nickel shot charged into the melt at refined-metal parity.
2025e annual average refined bismuth price, $20/lb (USGS MCS 2026).
